physicalNotes: Radius 1.58 Jupiter radii from Turner et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.485.5790T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract): 112,957.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.508 Jupiter masses (Turner et al. 2019, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2019MNRAS.485.5790T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.485.5790T/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): P 3.07172019 d
sources.shape: Turner et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.485.5790T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname TURNER_ET_AL__2019): a/R* 9.61; Turner et al. 2019 (2019MNRAS.485.5790T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname TURNER_ET_AL__2019): inclination 84.14 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458584.14248 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
